title: Settlement Record and the Escalation Rate on a Workplace Cafe Management Program Account
content:
Clause A — the term. Where the contract carries no late charge in the twenty-four months up to the day the invoice is raised and the payments received on the contract over the twelve months up to that day reach the management fees invoiced over those same twelve months, the escalation rate is the clean account escalation rate; where the contract carries no late charge over those twenty-four months and the payments received over those twelve months fall short of the management fees invoiced over them, the escalation rate is the partially settled escalation rate; and where the contract carries a late charge over those twenty-four months, the escalation rate is the annual price escalation printed against the service model.

Clause B — the rates written into the account terms. Under the Workplace Cafe Management Program the clean account escalation rate is 2.25 per cent and the partially settled escalation rate is 3.00 per cent. Where a late charge stands over those twenty-four months, no account term rate is written in and the rate is the annual price escalation printed against the service model.

Clause C — how the two windows are read. The late charge window is the twenty-four months up to the day the invoice is raised, and what is looked for in it is any late charge standing on the contract's ledger. The settlement window is the twelve months up to that same day, and the two quantities read over it are the payments received on the contract and the management fees invoiced on it. Payments that equal the management fees invoiced reach them; only payments below the management fees invoiced fall short.

Clause D — the term in tabular form.

| Late charges on the contract in the 24 months up to the day the invoice is raised | Payments received over the 12 months up to that day, against management fees invoiced over those 12 months | Escalation rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| None | Reach them | 2.25 per cent |
| None | Fall short of them | 3.00 per cent |
| One or more | Not in question | The annual price escalation printed against the service model |

Clause E — readings on hypothetical account records. A hypothetical account with no late charge over those 24 months, payments received of 61200.00 USD over those 12 months and management fees invoiced of 61200.00 USD over the same 12 months: the payments reach the management fees invoiced, and the escalation rate is 2.25 per cent. The same account with payments received of 61199.99 USD against management fees invoiced of 61200.00 USD: the payments fall short, and the escalation rate is 3.00 per cent. The same account carrying one late charge dated within those 24 months: the escalation rate is the annual price escalation printed against the service model, whatever the payments over the 12 months show.
